title: Rigging 12 non-humanoid creatures with code: 4 legs, 8 legs, no legs, wings and tentacles (84 animations)
author: Big-Communication950
selftext:
After my last post here, a commenter said the internet is full of humanoid packs and asked for non-humanoid ones. So I built 12 creatures where every body type needs a different rig: a wolf, boar and rat (four legs), a scorpion, beetle and crab (many legs), a viper (no legs), a toad (hops), a wasp and a floating eye (fly), a mushroom that waddles on two stubby legs, and a plant that walks on its roots.



How it works: everything is a Blender Python script written with Claude. The meshes are built from simple shapes, and every animation is key poses written in code. Some things I learned:



\- Four-legged walk: the feet lift off the floor when the legs swing, so the body has to dip by exactly the amount the leg arc shortens. Otherwise the wolf looks like it is skating.

\- Snake: a wave that travels from head to tail, with each bone turning a little later than the one before. The head turns the other way so it stays looking forward.

\- Overlap: tails, ears, wings and tentacles copy their parent's motion 3 frames late. That one trick does most of the "this looks alive" work.

\- Floor solver: after baking, a script checks the lowest point of every frame and lifts the body if anything goes under the floor.



The bugs were the fun part:

\- The toad's tongue attack pointed down into the floor, so the floor solver lifted the whole toad half a metre into the air.

\- The wasp's eyes and antennae floated 2 m above its head because I added the hover height twice.

\- My first beetle and crab had such long legs that they looked like spiders.



I review every clip as a frame strip. Each pack is also tested in Godot 4.7 and in Unity 6 (URP and Built-in) with a script that samples every clip on the skinned mesh. Procedural animation still isn't as good as a real animator, but for low poly enemies it holds up better than I expected.



If anyone wants to see them, the pack is here: [https://soresa-assets.itch.io/stylized-creatures](https://soresa-assets.itch.io/stylized-creatures)



Happy to answer questions about the rigs or the workflow. What body type would you find hardest to animate this way?
